skill.name: git-advanced
skill.description: Advanced Git workflow guidance for rebasing, conflict resolution, bisect debugging, reflog recovery, and branch management.
skill.summary: Plan and perform advanced Git workflows with safer recovery steps and clear command guidance.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily advanced Git documentation with one local Bash helper script. Static findings are mostly Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, and safe Git examples; the only confirmed issues are the presence of an executable helper script and its branch-deletion xargs path, which are intended but potentially destructive local operations.

remediation.issue: Executable helper script performs local destructive Git operations such as deleting merged branches.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to review the script before running it, keep confirmation prompts, and document that branch deletion and stash clearing can remove local work.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes many copyable commands that rewrite history, reset branches, force push, or clean files.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short safety preamble before destructive command sections that tells users to check status, create a backup branch, and confirm branch ownership.

remediation.issue: SSH troubleshooting example references a default private key path.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that users should only add their own key locally and should never paste private key contents into chat or logs.

static_findings.snippet: Follow these best practices to maintain clean Git history, avoid common pitfalls, and work effective
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v HEAD); do
git branch --merged | grep -v "\*\|main\|develop" | xargs -n 1 git branch -d
git branch --merged main | grep -v "^\*\|main\|develop" | xargs git branch -d
git branch | grep "feature/your-" | xargs git branch -d
git branch --merged main | grep -v "^\*\|main\|develop" | xargs git branch -d
# Rebase more frequently to avoid large divergence
for branch in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/); do
git branch --merged | grep -v "\*\|main\|master\|develop\|development" | xargs -r git branch -d

- `fixup` (f): Combine with previous commit, discard message

content.value_statement: Advanced Git tasks can damage history or slow teams when handled without a plan. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for rebases, conflicts, bisecting, recovery, and branch cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Explains interactive rebase workflows for squashing, reordering, editing, and dropping commits.
Guides merge conflict resolution with ours, theirs, manual merge, and mergetool strategies.
Shows how to use Git bisect manually or with a test script to locate regressions.
Provides reflog recovery steps for lost commits, dropped stashes, deleted branches, and bad resets.
Includes branch cleanup and management guidance for merged, stale, and archived branches.
Includes a local helper shell script for branch cleanup, conflict handling, rebasing, history viewing, and stash management.
limitations: It cannot know team branch policies unless the user provides them.
Some operations rewrite history or delete local Git state and need user confirmation.
Examples use placeholder repository URLs and file names that users must adapt.
The helper script works only in local Git repositories with standard Git commands available.

use_cases.title: Clean commits before review
use_cases.description: Use interactive rebase guidance to squash noisy commits, reorder changes, and prepare a readable pull request history.

use_cases.title: Resolve complex merge conflicts
use_cases.description: Compare both sides of a conflict, choose a safe resolution strategy, and continue merge, rebase, or cherry-pick operations.

use_cases.title: Recover lost Git work
use_cases.description: Use reflog, fsck, backup branches, and cherry-pick workflows to recover after bad resets, deleted branches, or failed rewrites.

prompt_templates.title: Explain my Git state
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me understand my current Git state. Ask me for the output of git status and git log if needed, then suggest the safest next command.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a clean rebase
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to clean up my feature branch before review. Help me plan an interactive rebase and list the safety checks before I run it.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a merge conflict
prompt_templates.scenario: User is blocked during merge or rebase
prompt_templates.prompt: I have merge conflicts. Guide me through identifying conflicted files, comparing ours and theirs, resolving safely, testing, and continuing the operation.

prompt_templates.title: Recover from a destructive Git mistake
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery after reset, force push, or deleted branch
prompt_templates.prompt: I may have lost commits after a Git operation. Help me use reflog and recovery branches without overwriting more history.

output_examples.input: I rebased and now my branch looks wrong.
output: Check git status first and avoid new resets.
Inspect git reflog to find the pre-rebase position.
Create a backup branch from the current state before restoring any older commit.

output_examples.input: I need to clean up ten commits before opening a pull request.
output: Start an interactive rebase against the base branch.
Squash fixup commits, reword unclear messages, and test before pushing with force-with-lease if appropriate.

output_examples.input: My merge has conflicts in several files.
output: Review each conflict with ours, theirs, and base views.
Resolve one file at a time, run tests, then continue the merge or rebase.

best_practices: Create a backup branch before rebases, resets, force pushes, or large cleanup operations.
Review both sides of each conflict and test the resolved code before continuing.
Use force-with-lease instead of force, and never rewrite shared branch history without team agreement.
anti_patterns: Running destructive Git commands before checking status, branch name, and reflog recovery options.
Accepting all ours or all theirs during conflicts without reviewing the affected code.
Copying placeholder commands without replacing branch names, repository URLs, and file paths.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill contains guidance and a helper script. Users should review commands before running them, especially commands that rewrite history or delete branches.

faq.question: Can it help with interactive rebase?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains rebase commands such as pick, reword, edit, squash, fixup, and drop, plus safety checks before pushing.

faq.question: Can it recover deleted branches?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides reflog-based recovery steps for deleted branches, lost commits, and dropped stashes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for shared production branches?
faq.answer: Use caution. The guidance repeatedly warns against rebasing or force pushing shared branches without coordination.

faq.question: Does it cover merge conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers conflict markers, ours and theirs strategies, manual resolution, merge tools, and testing after resolution.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
